commit_message:
[DispatchCreation] Skip split reduction candidates with unsupported combiners

SetSplitReductionSizesPass annotated every reduction that passed the size threshold, including reductions whose bodies the generic Linalg partial-reduction implementation cannot handle. For a coupled value/index argmax the index update depends on the value state, so matchReduction fails on that output and FormSplitReductionDispatches failed the whole compilation after the annotation had already been attached.

Check the conditions required by the generic implementation for each output before annotating: a single matched combiner and a known neutral element. Unsupported ops are left unsplit and continue through ordinary dispatch formation.

Fixes #25063.

Signed-off-by: losewayy <104015127+losewayy@users.noreply.github.com>
name: pr-greeter

commit_message:
[WebGPU] Retain builtin buffers until submission (#25068)

The builtin fill and unaligned-copy paths destroy their parameter
buffers before submitting the recorded commands. WebGPU then rejects the
submission with `Buffer used in submit while destroyed`.

This keeps those buffers alive until submission and cleans them up on
both success and error paths. I've checked direct execution and recorded
command replay in Chrome/WebGPU.

Signed-off-by: anutosh491 <andersonbhat491@gmail.com>
name: colab

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Make im2col a generic convolution rewrite (#25011)

Replaces the three layout-specific im2col patterns (NHWC, NCHW,
depthwise NHWC) with one generic rewrite that handles any convolution,
named or generic, including grouped, dilated, 1-D/3-D, dynamic and
integer ones.

The pattern gathers the convolved input with an all-parallel
`linalg.generic`, rewires the op to read the gather, keeps the original
payload, and collapses the result into a matmul using
`DispatchCreation::getCollapsibleLoops`. Add a basic heuristic via a
control function that skips convolutions without an output channel
dimension (depthwise, pooling), where the gather is never amortized.

The pass is renamed to `iree-global-opt-convert-conv-to-im2col`; the
pipeline flag is unchanged.

commit_message:
[WebGPU] Preserve Wasm host pointer widths (#25075)

I hit this while running JAX → IREE → WebGPU inside JupyterLite with
wasm64.

The WebGPU bridge passes host pointers as uint32_t and reads pointer
tables assuming four-byte entries. This truncates wasm64 addresses and
misreads multi-block instruction streams.

Use uintptr_t for host pointers and handle their width in JavaScript.
GPU handles and instruction words remain 32-bit. This also handles
signed wasm32 pointers above 2 GiB correctly.
Validates this for wasm32/wasm64.

Signed-off-by: anutosh491 <andersonbhat491@gmail.com>
name: setup / setup

[WebGPU] Preserve Wasm host pointer widths (#25075)

I hit this while running JAX → IREE → WebGPU inside JupyterLite with
wasm64.

The WebGPU bridge passes host pointers as uint32_t and reads pointer
tables assuming four-byte entries. This truncates wasm64 addresses and
misreads multi-block instruction streams.

Use uintptr_t for host pointers and handle their width in JavaScript.
GPU handles and instruction words remain 32-bit. This also handles
signed wasm32 pointers above 2 GiB correctly.
Validates this for wasm32/wasm64.

Signed-off-by: anutosh491 <andersonbhat491@gmail.com>
name: runtime :: macos-15

commit_message:
Integrate LLVM to llvm/llvm-project@03ddfac14e84 (#25082)

IREE has been adapted to the LLVM API changes (assisted by Claude Code,
manually reviewed):

Adaption in iree-tblgen source to definitions being a list of
definitions after 80017ba18d8c TableGen: Store classes and defs in a
StringMap (#231573).

Adaption to new header for arith::populateCeilFloorDivExpandOpsPatterns
after 076bd55e20d9 [mlir][Arith] Move ceil/floor div expansion to
Conversion/ArithCommon. NFC (#231064).

Support xnack on/off for ROCM gfx125x, following 05e432a8597f [AMDGPU]
Support xnack on/off on gfx125x (#232080). Remove the workaround that
always turns off XNACK for gfx1250.

Signed-off-by: Stefan Schuermans <schuermans@roofline.ai>
name: issue-greeter

commit_message:
[Util] Fix crash in MergeIndexSwitchPattern when second op yields outer values (#25038)

In `MergeIndexSwitchPattern`, remapping operands of the second
`scf.index_switch`'s yields used `IRMapping::lookupOrNull`. When a
yielded value was defined outside the switch region (e.g., hoisted
constants), it was absent from the mapper, resulting in a null operand
passed to `scf::YieldOp::create` and causing a crash.

Switch to `lookupOrDefault` for the second op's yielded values, matching
how the first op's yields are handled. Cloned values and results of the
first op are still remapped correctly, while values defined in enclosing
scopes pass through unchanged.

### Reproducer

Fails in `MergeIndexSwitchPattern::matchAndRewrite` →
`scf::YieldOp::create`:

```mlir
func.func @main(%sel: i32) -> (i32, i32) {
  %s = arith.index_cast %sel : i32 to index
  %a = scf.index_switch %s -> i32
  case 0 { %c = arith.constant 10 : i32
           scf.yield %c : i32 }
  case 1 { %c = arith.constant 11 : i32
           scf.yield %c : i32 }
  default { %c = arith.constant 12 : i32
            scf.yield %c : i32 }
  %b = scf.index_switch %s -> i32
  case 0 { %c = arith.constant 20 : i32
           scf.yield %c : i32 }
  case 1 { %c = arith.constant 21 : i32
           scf.yield %c : i32 }
  default { %c = arith.constant 22 : i32
            scf.yield %c : i32 }
  return %a, %b : i32, i32
}
```

```shell
iree-compile repro.mlir --iree-hal-target-device=local \
  --iree-hal-local-target-device-backends=vmvx -o /dev/null
```

### Changes

- Use `IRMapping::lookupOrDefault` when resolving yielded values from
the second switch.
- Add a regression test in `Dialect/Util/Transforms/test/patterns.mlir`
covering outer-scope yield values.

[Util] Fix crash in MergeIndexSwitchPattern when second op yields outer values (#25038)

In `MergeIndexSwitchPattern`, remapping operands of the second
`scf.index_switch`'s yields used `IRMapping::lookupOrNull`. When a
yielded value was defined outside the switch region (e.g., hoisted
constants), it was absent from the mapper, resulting in a null operand
passed to `scf::YieldOp::create` and causing a crash.

Switch to `lookupOrDefault` for the second op's yielded values, matching
how the first op's yields are handled. Cloned values and results of the
first op are still remapped correctly, while values defined in enclosing
scopes pass through unchanged.

### Reproducer

Fails in `MergeIndexSwitchPattern::matchAndRewrite` →
`scf::YieldOp::create`:

```mlir
func.func @main(%sel: i32) -> (i32, i32) {
  %s = arith.index_cast %sel : i32 to index
  %a = scf.index_switch %s -> i32
  case 0 { %c = arith.constant 10 : i32
           scf.yield %c : i32 }
  case 1 { %c = arith.constant 11 : i32
           scf.yield %c : i32 }
  default { %c = arith.constant 12 : i32
            scf.yield %c : i32 }
  %b = scf.index_switch %s -> i32
  case 0 { %c = arith.constant 20 : i32
           scf.yield %c : i32 }
  case 1 { %c = arith.constant 21 : i32
           scf.yield %c : i32 }
  default { %c = arith.constant 22 : i32
            scf.yield %c : i32 }
  return %a, %b : i32, i32
}
```

```shell
iree-compile repro.mlir --iree-hal-target-device=local \
  --iree-hal-local-target-device-backends=vmvx -o /dev/null
```

### Changes

- Use `IRMapping::lookupOrDefault` when resolving yielded values from
the second switch.
- Add a regression test in `Dialect/Util/Transforms/test/patterns.mlir`
covering outer-scope yield values.

Assisted-by: Claude Code

Signed-off-by: jonathansong <7958352+jonathansong@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: jonathansong <7958352+jonathansong@users.noreply.github.com>

In `MergeIndexSwitchPattern`, remapping operands of the second
`scf.index_switch`'s yields used `IRMapping::lookupOrNull`. When a

commit_message:
[Util] Ensure scf.index_switch ops share the same selector before merging (#25037)

`MergeIndexSwitchPattern` merges adjacent `scf.index_switch` operations
when their case values match, but it fails to verify that both ops
switch on the same condition operand (selector). Consequently, the
merged operation retains only the first op's selector, causing the
second op's regions to execute based on the wrong value.

### Minimal reproducer

Run with `iree-opt --iree-util-apply-patterns
--allow-unregistered-dialect`:

```mlir
util.func @f(%case0: index, %case1: index) -> (i32, i32) {
  %result0 = scf.index_switch %case0 -> i32
  case 0 { %v = "some.op0.case0"() : () -> i32
           scf.yield %v : i32 }
  case 1 { %v = "some.op0.case1"() : () -> i32
           scf.yield %v : i32 }
  default { %v = "some.op0.default"() : () -> i32
            scf.yield %v : i32 }
  %result1 = scf.index_switch %case1 -> i32
  case 0 { %v = "some.op1.case0"() : () -> i32
           scf.yield %v : i32 }
  case 1 { %v = "some.op1.case1"() : () -> i32
           scf.yield %v : i32 }
  default { %v = "some.op1.default"() : () -> i32
            scf.yield %v : i32 }
  util.return %result0, %result1 : i32, i32
}
```

Prior to this fix, the pattern collapses both into a single
`scf.index_switch %case0 -> i32, i32`, silently discarding `%case1`.

### Changes

- Require matching selector operands in `MergeIndexSwitchPattern` before
merging.
- Add a negative test case to
`Dialect/Util/Transforms/test/patterns.mlir` to ensure distinct
selectors prevent merging.

Assisted-by: Claude Code

`MergeIndexSwitchPattern` merges adjacent `scf.index_switch` operations
when their case values match, but it fails to verify that both ops
switch on the same condition operand (selector). Consequently, the
merged operation retains only the first op's selector, causing the
second op's regions to execute based on the wrong value.

### Minimal reproducer

Run with `iree-opt --iree-util-apply-patterns
--allow-unregistered-dialect`:

```mlir

  %result0 = scf.index_switch %case0 -> i32
  case 0 { %v = "some.op0.case0"() : () -> i32
           scf.yield %v : i32 }
  case 1 { %v = "some.op0.case1"() : () -> i32
           scf.yield %v : i32 }
  default { %v = "some.op0.default"() : () -> i32
            scf.yield %v : i32 }
  %result1 = scf.index_switch %case1 -> i32
  case 0 { %v = "some.op1.case0"() : () -> i32
           scf.yield %v : i32 }
  case 1 { %v = "some.op1.case1"() : () -> i32
           scf.yield %v : i32 }
  default { %v = "some.op1.default"() : () -> i32
            scf.yield %v : i32 }
  util.return %result0, %result1 : i32, i32
}
```

Prior to this fix, the pattern collapses both into a single
`scf.index_switch %case0 -> i32, i32`, silently discarding `%case1`.

`Dialect/Util/Transforms/test/patterns.mlir` to ensure distinct

[Util] Ensure scf.index_switch ops share the same selector before merging (#25037)

`MergeIndexSwitchPattern` merges adjacent `scf.index_switch` operations
when their case values match, but it fails to verify that both ops
switch on the same condition operand (selector). Consequently, the
merged operation retains only the first op's selector, causing the
second op's regions to execute based on the wrong value.

### Minimal reproducer

Run with `iree-opt --iree-util-apply-patterns
--allow-unregistered-dialect`:

```mlir
util.func @f(%case0: index, %case1: index) -> (i32, i32) {
  %result0 = scf.index_switch %case0 -> i32
  case 0 { %v = "some.op0.case0"() : () -> i32
           scf.yield %v : i32 }
  case 1 { %v = "some.op0.case1"() : () -> i32
           scf.yield %v : i32 }
  default { %v = "some.op0.default"() : () -> i32
            scf.yield %v : i32 }
  %result1 = scf.index_switch %case1 -> i32
  case 0 { %v = "some.op1.case0"() : () -> i32
           scf.yield %v : i32 }
  case 1 { %v = "some.op1.case1"() : () -> i32
           scf.yield %v : i32 }
  default { %v = "some.op1.default"() : () -> i32
            scf.yield %v : i32 }
  util.return %result0, %result1 : i32, i32
}
```

Prior to this fix, the pattern collapses both into a single
`scf.index_switch %case0 -> i32, i32`, silently discarding `%case1`.

### Changes

- Require matching selector operands in `MergeIndexSwitchPattern` before
merging.
- Add a negative test case to
`Dialect/Util/Transforms/test/patterns.mlir` to ensure distinct
selectors prevent merging.

Assisted-by: Claude Code

Signed-off-by: jonathansong <7958352+jonathansong@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-authored-by: jonathansong <7958352+jonathansong@users.noreply.github.com>

commit_message:
[SPIRV] Unroll wide elementwise vector operations (#25053)

I hit this while compiling a JAX training step to WebGPU through IREE in
the browser.

A `vector<32xf32>` addition survived until SPIR-V conversion and caused
compilation to fail. This uses MLIR's existing unrolling patterns in the
vector-breakdown pass to split wide elementwise operations into
four-element operations.

Signed-off-by: anutosh491 <andersonbhat491@gmail.com>
name: setup / setup

I hit this while compiling a JAX training step to WebGPU through IREE in
the browser.

A `vector<32xf32>` addition survived until SPIR-V conversion and caused
compilation to fail. This uses MLIR's existing unrolling patterns in the
vector-breakdown pass to split wide elementwise operations into
four-element operations.

Signed-off-by: anutosh491 <andersonbhat491@gmail.com>
name: Test ONNX / test_onnx_models :: amdgpu_hip_rdna4

commit_message:
Integrate LLVM to llvm/llvm-project@03ddfac14e84

IREE has been adapted to the LLVM API changes (assisted by Claude Code, manually reviewed):

Adaption in iree-tblgen source to definitions being a list of definitions after
80017ba18d8c TableGen: Store classes and defs in a StringMap (#231573).

Adaption to new header for arith::populateCeilFloorDivExpandOpsPatterns after
076bd55e20d9 [mlir][Arith] Move ceil/floor div expansion to Conversion/ArithCommon. NFC (#231064).

Support xnack on/off for ROCM gfx125x, following
05e432a8597f [AMDGPU] Support xnack on/off on gfx125x (#232080).
Remove the workaround that always turns off XNACK for gfx1250.

Signed-off-by: Stefan Schuermans <schuermans@roofline.ai>
name: pre-commit

Integrate LLVM to llvm/llvm-project@03ddfac14e84

IREE has been adapted to the LLVM API changes (assisted by Claude Code, manually reviewed):

Adaption in iree-tblgen source to definitions being a list of definitions after
80017ba18d8c TableGen: Store classes and defs in a StringMap (#231573).

Adaption to new header for arith::populateCeilFloorDivExpandOpsPatterns after
076bd55e20d9 [mlir][Arith] Move ceil/floor div expansion to Conversion/ArithCommon. NFC (#231064).

Support xnack on/off for ROCM gfx125x, following
05e432a8597f [AMDGPU] Support xnack on/off on gfx125x (#232080).
Remove the workaround that always turns off XNACK for gfx1250.

commit_message:
[GlobalOptimization] Make im2col a generic convolution rewrite (#25011)

Replaces the three layout-specific im2col patterns (NHWC, NCHW,
depthwise NHWC) with one generic rewrite that handles any convolution,
named or generic, including grouped, dilated, 1-D/3-D, dynamic and
integer ones.

The pattern gathers the convolved input with an all-parallel
`linalg.generic`, rewires the op to read the gather, keeps the original
payload, and collapses the result into a matmul using
`DispatchCreation::getCollapsibleLoops`. Add a basic heuristic via a
control function that skips convolutions without an output channel
dimension (depthwise, pooling), where the gather is never amortized.

The pass is renamed to `iree-global-opt-convert-conv-to-im2col`; the
pipeline flag is unchanged.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

---------

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Replaces the three layout-specific im2col patterns (NHWC, NCHW,
depthwise NHWC) with one generic rewrite that handles any convolution,
named or generic, including grouped, dilated, 1-D/3-D, dynamic and
integer ones.

The pattern gathers the convolved input with an all-parallel
`linalg.generic`, rewires the op to read the gather, keeps the original
payload, and collapses the result into a matmul using
`DispatchCreation::getCollapsibleLoops`. Add a basic heuristic via a
control function that skips convolutions without an output channel
dimension (depthwise, pooling), where the gather is never amortized.

The pass is renamed to `iree-global-opt-convert-conv-to-im2col`; the
pipeline flag is unchanged.

commit_message:
[WebGPU] Retain builtin buffers until submission (#25068)

The builtin fill and unaligned-copy paths destroy their parameter
buffers before submitting the recorded commands. WebGPU then rejects the
submission with `Buffer used in submit while destroyed`.

This keeps those buffers alive until submission and cleans them up on
both success and error paths. I've checked direct execution and recorded
command replay in Chrome/WebGPU.

Signed-off-by: anutosh491 <andersonbhat491@gmail.com>
